_comment: Provider and model registry. Swapping a model is a config change, not a code change. Rates are USD per million tokens.

bedrock.note: us.* cross-region inference profiles, US East. Carries a ~10% premium over global.* for resilience across three US regions. Serves the apps (see serving_provider) since 2026-09-04, when the opus-5 entitlement arrived.

anthropic.note: The frontier comparison, and the fallback route to opus-5 should Bedrock lose the entitlement. Billing goes to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local and nowhere else -- host-managed CLI credentials are stripped from the subprocess (host_managed_auth_env below), because they once silently served every call on this provider.

_host_managed_auth_env_comment: Credential channels the Claude Code CLI can authenticate through BESIDES the provider's own credential_env. Stripped from every resolver subprocess. This list exists because it was not stripped: in a managed container the CLI carries host-managed session credentials (CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1 plus an OAuth token), preferred them over ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and $8.96 of 'anthropic' spend was actually billed to the session's own account -- the console for the project's key showed zero, and an EXPIRED key appeared to work. With these stripped, the provider named on a model in this file is exactly who gets billed. See results/notes/anthropic-billing-postmortem.md.
_subprocess_env_allowlist_comment: DEFAULT-DENY: the resolver's CLI subprocess is exec'd (tools/cli_guard.py) with ONLY these variables plus the selected provider's credential_env and env flags. A denylist was tried twice and failed twice -- first the SDK's env overlay resurrected popped keys, then the CLI authenticated from its on-disk login (~/.claude.json oauthAccount) with every env channel closed. The guard also gives the CLI a private empty HOME and closes inherited file descriptors. host_managed_auth_env above is kept as belt-and-braces blanking for the same variables. Behavioural proof: tools/anthropic_auth_probe.py step 1.

opus-5-bedrock.rates_note: First-party opus-5 rates x1.1, the same us.* regional premium the other Bedrock entries carry.
opus-5-bedrock.tokenizer_note: 4.7-and-later tokenizer: ~30% more tokens for the same text than 4.6. Token counts are therefore NOT directly comparable to the 4.6 runs; cost is.
opus-5-bedrock.note: Serves the apps (see serving_provider). The opus-5 Bedrock entitlement arrived 2026-09-04 -- tools/bedrock_preflight.py now reports SUCCESS for us.anthropic.claude-opus-5 -- so serving moved here from the first-party API: same model, billed to the AWS credits.

opus-5.rates_note: Claude API first-party, global routing (no 1.1x us data-residency multiplier; the Bedrock entries above carry their own 1.1x regional premium). Read from platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing on 2026-08-13.
opus-5.tokenizer_note: 4.7-and-later tokenizer: ~30% more tokens for the same text than 4.6. Token counts are therefore NOT directly comparable to the 4.6 runs; cost is. The comparison report must say which it is reporting.
opus-5.note: The frontier-comparison configuration, via the first-party Anthropic API. Scored 93.3% on both input formats. Serving moved to opus-5-bedrock on 2026-09-04 when the Bedrock entitlement arrived; this entry remains the comparison record and the fallback route to the same model.

sonnet-5.rates_note: Same source and date. The $2/$10 introductory rate is now the standard price; the scheduled 2026-09-01 rise to $3/$15 was cancelled.
sonnet-5.tokenizer_note: 4.7-and-later tokenizer: ~30% more tokens for the same text than 4.6. Token counts are therefore NOT directly comparable to the 4.6 runs; cost is. The comparison report must say which it is reporting.
sonnet-5.note: Anthropic API only. NOT entitled on this Bedrock account (tools/bedrock_preflight.py reports NOT-ENTITLED).

_serving_provider_comment: The one provider the operator and internal apps may spend on. config.check_default() refuses to start an app whose default model is served by anything else -- a default the deployment cannot run must fail at startup, not four retries into the first denial an operator submits. Eval runs are unaffected: they name their model explicitly and gate on that model's own provider budget.

default._comment: What the apps serve denials with. opus-5 at high effort, on Umer's instruction -- the strongest model measured (93.3% on both formats) -- served through Bedrock since 2026-09-04, when the entitlement arrived and the AWS credits became the cheaper route to the same model. Changing it is a config change, not a code change -- and it is invisible to the operator app either way, which has no model control by design.
